rektion: etw. (Akk.) hinunterfallen (die Treppe hinunterfallen); von etw. hinunterfallen
definition_de: von oben nach unten fallen (ugs.: runterfallen); mit Akkusativ für den Weg: die Treppe hinunterfallen
example_de: Der schwere Koffer ist die ganze Treppe hinuntergefallen und unten aufgesprungen.
example_en: The heavy suitcase fell all the way down the stairs and burst open at the bottom.
user_example_de: Mein Großvater ist die Treppe hinuntergefallen.
visual_idea: Same pattern as the user's sentence ('die Treppe hinunterfallen', Akk. for the path): a suitcase lies burst open at the bottom of an Altbau staircase while its owner stares down from the top. The result state is reliable to draw; the fall itself is in the video.
image_prompt: an old wooden staircase in a German Altbau stairwell seen from below, a large suitcase lying burst open on the bottom steps with clothes, shoes and a towel scattered across the last stairs and the floor, a young man standing at the top of the stairs with both hands on his head in shock, warm light from a tall window
negative_prompt: text, letters, watermark, signature, caption, blurry, extra fingers, deformed hands, cluttered background, multiple panels
